question: Compare maize and soybean: what does each need?

answer:
Maize and soybean share similar temperature and rainfall needs, but differ in their specific soil pH and growing cycle ranges [S1]. Both crops thrive under very bright light and prefer high soil fertility with low salinity [S1].

For temperature, maize requires an optimal mean of 18-33 °C and tolerates 10-47 °C, while soybean prefers 20-33 °C and tolerates 10-38 °C [S1]. Annual rainfall requirements are also close, with maize needing an optimal 600-1200 mm (tolerated 400-1800 mm) and soybean needing 600-1500 mm (tolerated 450-1800 mm) [S1].

Soil pH preferences differ slightly: maize has an optimal range of 5-7 (tolerated 4.5-8.5), whereas soybean prefers 5.5-6.5 (tolerated 4.5-8.4) [S1]. Furthermore, maize has a wider growing period of 65-365 days compared to soybean's 75-180 days [S1].
